data_handling: GitLab Support policy context (paraphrase). Data classification describes the sensitivity of information; a system's classification describes the levels it may handle. Do not transfer information into a system whose approved level is lower than the information's level. System approval alone does not authorize every disclosure: ORANGE information must not be posted publicly even in a RED-approved system. Use confidential visibility where needed and limit access to authorized recipients. Published tool classifications are examples; the organization's Tech Stack is the authority. For this hypothetical question, use classifications explicitly stated to have been verified; do not guess omitted classifications, visibility, or authorization. Assess only these named requirements, not unrelated workflow rules.
support_exception: GitLab customer-support exception (paraphrase). RED customer data is generally barred from unapproved systems. Team members may move it to a GitLab-managed laptop specifically for customer support on an active support case. The exception requires deletion immediately after case resolution and recording all handling in the ZenDesk ticket. On macOS, deletion must include clearing Trash or bypassing Trash. Other business purposes are outside this exception and require a separate exception process. Evaluate eligibility for this particular exception before migration, using stated commitments to future deletion and documentation; do not claim those obligations have already been performed. An unspecified logging destination is not evidence that the required ZenDesk documentation will occur. Missing required facts remain unresolved, while an explicit disqualifying fact can establish failure of this exception. These rules concern GitLab, not an unrelated organization.
